answer: Neighborhood genus gate. Each agent keeps a local vertex neighborhood; admission requires its induced subgraph's genus to stay at or below a fixed bound, computed as the Euler-characteristic kernel of that subgraph. The velvet rule: an identity whose neighborhood merges two previously separate clusters raises local genus and is rejected by peers running the check. An attacker must build many genuine, topologically distinct neighborhoods and sustain their edges, paying real compute and connectivity per identity.
